:::{#thm-double-complement}
#### The orthogonal complement of the orthogonal complement

For any subspace $\mathcal{S}$ of $\reals^p$,

$$
(\mathcal{S}^\perp)^\perp = \mathcal{S}.
$$

:::

::: proof

**$\mathcal{S} \subseteq (\mathcal{S}^\perp)^\perp$.**
Take $\vecf{s} \in \mathcal{S}$ and any $\vecf{v} \in \mathcal{S}^\perp$.
By @def-orthogonal-complement, $\vecf{s} \cdot \vecf{v} = 0$,
so $\vecf{v} \cdot \vecf{s} = 0$ too (@thm-lincom-symmetric).
So $\vecf{s}$ is orthogonal to every vector of $\mathcal{S}^\perp$,
that is, $\vecf{s} \in (\mathcal{S}^\perp)^\perp$.

**Equal dimensions.**
$\mathcal{S}^\perp$ is a subspace (@thm-orthogonal-complement-subspace),
so part 2 of @thm-orthogonal-direct-sum applies to it as well as to $\mathcal{S}$:

$$
\ba
\dim\paren{(\mathcal{S}^\perp)^\perp}
&= p - \dim(\mathcal{S}^\perp)
&& \text{(@thm-orthogonal-direct-sum, applied to } \mathcal{S}^\perp \text{)}
\\
&= p - \paren{p - \dim(\mathcal{S})}
&& \text{(@thm-orthogonal-direct-sum, applied to } \mathcal{S} \text{)}
\\
&= \dim(\mathcal{S}).
&& \text{(arithmetic)}
\ea
$$

$(\mathcal{S}^\perp)^\perp$ is a subspace (@thm-orthogonal-complement-subspace)
that contains $\mathcal{S}$ and has the same dimension,
so it equals $\mathcal{S}$ (@thm-subspace-equal-dim).

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-double-complement}
#### Back to the line

In @exm-orthogonal-direct-sum,
$\mathcal{S} = \operatorname{span}\cb{(1, 1, 0)}$
and $\mathcal{S}^\perp = \operatorname{span}\cb{(1, -1, 0), (0, 0, 1)}$.
Put those two spanning vectors in the columns of the $3 \times 2$ matrix
$\matr{B} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$,
so $\mathcal{S}^\perp = \mathcal{C}(\matr{B})$ (@thm-column-space-span)
and $(\mathcal{S}^\perp)^\perp = \mathcal{N}(\tp{\matr{B}})$ (@thm-complement-null-space).
Since $\tp{\matr{B}} \vecf{w} = (w_1 - w_2,\ w_3)$ (@def-matvec-mult),
$\vecf{w} \in (\mathcal{S}^\perp)^\perp$
exactly when $w_1 - w_2 = 0$ and $w_3 = 0$.
So $(\mathcal{S}^\perp)^\perp = \cb{(a, a, 0) : a \in \reals} = \mathcal{S}$.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-double-complement-fails}
#### A set that is not a subspace does not come back

The one-element set $\mathcal{X} = \cb{(1, 1, 0)}$ is not a subspace.
Its orthogonal complement is the same as that of $\mathcal{S}$ in @exm-double-complement,
since both are defined by the single condition $u_1 + u_2 = 0$,
so $(\mathcal{X}^\perp)^\perp = \operatorname{span}\cb{(1, 1, 0)}$,
which contains $(2, 2, 0) \notin \mathcal{X}$.
@thm-double-complement needs $\mathcal{S}$ to be a subspace.

:::
